properties.species: Cr2, X 1Sigma_g+ (formal sextuple bond), charge 0, multiplicity 1, gas phase
properties.level_of_theory: Gaussian 16 RevC.01, PM7 semiempirical, gas phase (no solvent, no counterions)
properties.bond_dissociation_energy_definition: De of the same-surface PM7 potential energy curve: E(Cr2, R = 8.000 A asymptote) - E(Cr2, PM7 equilibrium minimum at R = 2.468 A). D0 = De - ZPE (835.6 cm-1 -> 1.19 kcal/mol).
properties.bond_dissociation_energy_atom_reference_: Extension only: 2 x E(Cr atom, PM7, septet) - E(Cr2 minimum) = 312.8 kcal/mol. PM7 puts the two isolated Cr atoms ~0.50 hartree ABOVE its own Cr2 asymptote, an internal inconsistency of the method; this number is NOT the delivered BDE.

potential_energy_curve.description: Rigid PM7 potential energy curve of Cr2: Cr-Cr distance constrained, independent Gaussian single point with a fresh SCF guess at every distance (charge 0, multiplicity 1). The equilibrium point is the PM7 optimum R = 2.4679 A.
potential_energy_curve.units: bond_length_angstrom / energy_hartree / relative_energy_kcal_mol (relative to the PM7 minimum)

properties.comparison_to_experiment: Experimental: D0(Cr2) = 1.44 +/- 0.06 eV = 33.2 kcal/mol, re = 1.679 A. PM7 gives a bound Cr2 with D0 = 25.6 kcal/mol (about 8 kcal/mol too weak) but re = 2.468 A, i.e. 0.79 A too long, and a very soft 836 cm-1 mode. PM7 therefore reproduces the existence and the order of magnitude of the Cr-Cr bond but is not a quantitative description of the sextuple bond.
properties.cross_check_xtb_gfn2: GFN2-xTB (xtb 6.5.0, single point at R = 2.45 A): E = -3.703290 Eh versus 2 x E(Cr) = -3.494995 Eh, i.e. ~131 kcal/mol at that unrelaxed geometry - xTB overbinds far more strongly than PM7 and also fails quantitatively. xtb output is not an accepted evidence format for this task, so it is reported as a cross-check only.
properties.caveats: Single-reference semiempirical SCF supports several self-consistent solutions for Cr2. At R = 2.70-2.90 A a second closed-shell solution 0.07-0.13 hartree lower is found, and an optimisation started at R = 2.90 A runs to R = 4.013 A (E = 0.668221 hartree, one 27.1 cm-1 mode); that branch is separated by a ~0.18 hartree discontinuity and is discarded as an SCF artefact. Only the smooth, reproducible branch (rigid scan, independent single points and the optimisation from R = 2.45 A, all in agreement) is delivered. A true description of the Cr2 sextuple bond requires multireference (CASSCF/MRCI) treatment, which is outside the allowed methods (xTB, PM7).

properties.species: two separated Cr atoms, charge 0, multiplicity 7 (2 x 7S3, d5s1) - the true ground-state dissociation products
properties.level_of_theory: Gaussian 16 RevC.01, PM7 semiempirical, gas phase
properties.note: The adiabatic dissociation products of ground-state Cr2 are two 7S Cr atoms; the closed-shell singlet Cr2 surface is not adiabatically connected to them, so the delivered BDE is taken from the same-surface PM7 asymptote (0.843903 hartree at R = 8.0 A), not from these atomic energies.

edges.channel: Cr-Cr bond dissociation (homolysis of the formal sextuple bond); monotonic and barrierless on the PM7 curve
edges.note: A diatomic has a single internal coordinate, so no transition state and no barrier exist on the Cr2 -> 2 Cr path. The edge is a barrierless bond-cleavage step and deliberately carries no barrier_kcal_mol.
